title: Daniel Radcliffe and the Art of Playing a "Weird Little Guy"
summary:
A film writer says there is a fun way to see how far Daniel Radcliffe has come since he starred in the Harry Potter movies. In an opinion piece, the writer recommends the 2016 movie "Swiss Army Man," which is now streaming on Netflix. The film was written and directed by Daniel Scheinert and Daniel Kwan, known as "the Daniels," who later made "Everything Everywhere All at Once." Paul Dano also stars. The writer calls the movie "absolutely wild in the best way" and says it is an important part of Radcliffe's growth as an actor.

The writer also uses the internet phrase "weird little guy." It describes an actor who can turn into strange, unusual characters. The writer says it is about a state of mind, not size, and gives Nicholas Hoult, Robert Pattinson and Alexander Skarsgård as examples. Radcliffe, the writer says, is a great example too.

According to the writer, Radcliffe has worked hard since Harry Potter to avoid being tied to that role. His roles include a man who grows horns in "Horns," a sneaky villain in "Now You See Me 2" and "The Lost City," and a heightened version of musician "Weird Al" Yankovic in "Weird: The Al Yankovic Story."

Radcliffe has also done a lot of stage work, in shows such as "Equus" and "How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying." He won his first Tony Award for a Broadway revival of "Merrily We Roll Along." On television, he starred in "Miracle Workers." In 2026 he stars with Tracy Morgan in a comedy called "The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins," which the writer praises as one of the best comedies on air.
why_it_matters: It shows how actors can grow past one famous role, and readers can use the writer's view to pick something new to watch.
